entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Patna
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned A.P.P. for the State.
2. The petitioner apprehends his arrest in connection with Mahila P.S. Case No. 43 of 2022 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 341, 323, 379 and 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

3. The learned Counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner had earlier moved before this Court seeking anticipatory bail by filing Cr. Misc. No. 40285 of 2023 and the same was disposed of on 13.02.2024 in terms of order dated 13.02.2024 in Cr. Misc. No. 3536 of 2024 in Naushad Ansari V. The State of Bihar.

entities.text: Naushad Ansari V. The State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned Counsel next submits that the police after investigation has submitted the charge-sheet, as such the second anticipatory bail has been filed .

It is further Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.61351 of 2024(2) dt.05-02-2025 submitted that during the course of investigation the police never felt the need of arresting the petitioner, as such no useful purpose would be served by sending the petitioner in jail.
It is also submitted that the dispute is completely matrimonial.
4. The learned Counsel for the petitioner next submits that the case be referred for mediation on which the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the O.P. No. 2 also agrees.

sentences.text: In view of the joint submission made by the learned Counsels for the parties, the case is referred for mediation, as such the petitioner and the O.P. No. 2 are directed to remain physically present before the Mediation Center of the Patna High Court on 17.02.2025, so that the case is referred to the learned Mediator for resolving the dispute amicably.
There shall be no coercive steps taken against the petitioner until the anticipatory bail application is finally adjudicated by this Court.
